title: World amulet node record
description: One record per node of the world's amulet practice: a kind of amulet, a tradition that carries it, a motif cut into it, a material it is made from, a practice that makes or charges or retires it, a place, a person, an organization, a word, a picture, or a long read. The tradition's own term is the identity. Every field carries provenance (record default + per-field override). Keys beginning with x_ are free extension slots and are never rejected.

name.description: what the tradition calls it, in English or in romanisation

native.description: the name in its own script

script.description: the script `native` is written in: Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, Han, Hebrew, Greek, Cyrillic, Ge'ez, Hiragana, hieroglyphic

lang.description: BCP-47-ish language tag for `native`, e.g. ar, th, he, ja, am

said.description: how it is said out loud where it is used

th.description: the name in Thai, for the Thai edition; for a Thai practice the same as `native`

root.description: the etymon or morpheme chain, e.g. Latin amuletum > French amulette > English amulet

first_attested.description: earliest dated use you can NAME with a source; blank if none

folk.description: a folk etymology, labelled as one

region.description: open list, validated against data/vocab/regions.json with a warning

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the practice is documented in; drives the world map

facets.description: open per-type facets; scalars or lists. Known keys per type in data/vocab/facets.json

what.description: one plain paragraph: what it is

story.description: narrative, told as narrative; source marks inline: *Tradition holds —* / *Inference —*

how.description: how it is made, charged, worn, kept, retired

text_th.description: the Thai edition's text, written in Thai, same sections as `text`; a section left out shows the English with a note

th_fields.description: Thai for the short structured fields, keyed by path: etymology.root, dating.note, object.made_by, against.0.who, confusable_with.1.tell, sections.0.h …; a path left out shows the English

kin.description: what other nodes ARE to this one, said from here. Directional: the other record says its own sentence back.

dating.description: When the thing is attested. Years are astronomical integers: 1 CE is 1, 1 BCE is 0, 500 BCE is -499. Use `label` for how a reader should read it.

period.description: the period name a museum label would print, e.g. Middle Kingdom, Late Roman, Edo

to_year.description: latest attested; null means still in use

living.description: true where people still carry it as of the `updated` date

label.description: the span in words, e.g. 'c. 2000 BCE to the present'

object.description: The physical thing, described the way a catalogue card describes it. Any field nobody publishes stays null or absent — never estimated here.

form.description: key from data/vocab/forms.json: pendant, ring, bead, plaque, scroll, packet, knot, cord, coin, figurine, tattoo, nail, mirror, bell, bag, tablet, card, sticker

worn.description: keys from data/vocab/worn.json: neck, wrist, upper-arm, ankle, waist, hair, ear, pocket, sewn-in, door, vehicle, boat, foundation, grave, shop, field, cradle, phone

made_by.description: who is entitled to make it, in the tradition's own terms

inscription.description: what is written on it, in translation; put the script in `script`

length_mm.description: typical longest dimension, only where a source publishes one

count.description: where the tradition specifies a number — beads, knots, folds

single_use.description: true where it is retired or burnt after a term

against.description: What the tradition says it is for. Reported, never adjudicated. Keys from data/vocab/against.json.

who.description: whose claim this is: the maker, a text, wearers, an ethnographer

quote.description: the claim in somebody's own words, in quotation marks, attributed

holdings.description: Where examples can be seen. An accession number goes in ONLY when read off a published catalogue entry; otherwise leave it out.

open_access.description: true where the museum publishes its images under an open licence

restricted.description: Set where a tradition restricts what outsiders may be told or shown. The site prints the note instead of the detail, and the detail does not get written.

fields.description: dotted field path -> provenance override, e.g. text.story

tags.description: Claims about a place a reader might pick it by. Every tag names its evidence.

recognitions.description: Named recognitions by others. Counted, never weighted by this project.

sections.description: Long-form pieces (type story, art): headed sections rendered in order after text.what

hours.description: When a place is open, as days. A day in `open` is open; a day in `closed` is closed; a day in NEITHER is not known, which is never the same thing as closed.
